lines: A physically modelled Wurlitzer 200A electric piano: sixteen voices of reed and electrostatic pickup through a preamp, power amp and speaker, then tremolo, auto-pan, chorus and a low-pass filter
Scales the drive into the pickup's nonlinearity: below the midpoint it tames the per-key calibrated amount toward nothing, at the midpoint it is that amount, and fully up it is 1.5 times it
Trims the level into the preamp saturation stage, -12dB to +12dB, with the level compensated afterwards so the change is heard mostly as timbre
Sets the master level on a squared taper; whether the panel envelope also shapes the amplitude is picked on this knob's own right-click menu
Sets the attack time of the panel envelope, 0.5ms at the left to 5 seconds at the right
Sets the decay time of the panel envelope, 5ms at the left to 5 seconds at the right
Sets the level the panel envelope holds while a note is held down, 0 to 100%
Sets the release time of the panel envelope, 5ms at the left to 5 seconds at the right
Sets how deep the tremolo modulates the amplitude, 0 to 100%; at 0% the tremolo is off
Sets the tremolo rate: with CLOCK empty a free-running period from 0.05 seconds to 5 seconds, and with a clock patched one of fifteen ratios of it from /16 to x16
Sets how far the auto-pan swings the signal between the two outputs, 0 to 100%; at 0% both outputs carry the same level
Sets the auto-pan rate: with CLOCK empty a free-running period from 0.05 seconds to 5 seconds, and with a clock patched one of fifteen ratios of it from /16 to x16
Sets the cutoff of the low-pass filter the whole output runs through, 20Hz to 20000Hz
Sets the filter's Q, 0.5 at the left to 10 at the right
Sets the chorus LFO rate, 0.05Hz to 8Hz
Sets how far the chorus LFO sweeps its delay time, 0 to 100%
Sets the chorus delay time the LFO sweeps around, 1ms to 20ms
Mixes the chorus against the dry signal on an equal-power curve; at 0% the chorus is bypassed and costs no processing
The pitch of each voice, read once as the gate for that channel rises and rounded to the nearest semitone; after the strike only BEND moves that note
A rising gate here strikes a note on that channel and a falling gate damps it; the number of channels patched here sets how many of the sixteen voices run
Sets how hard each note is struck, 0V for the softest strike and 10V for the hardest; with nothing patched every note strikes at full
A modulation voltage for the bark amount and for the reed drive, read per channel; each of those reads it only while its own menu is set to Mod input
A gate above 2V holds the notes that are playing, freezing the reed decay in Reed mode and holding the envelope's segment in Envelope mode; the notes damp when it falls
Bends every sounding note, with ±5V covering the full bend either way; how many semitones that is comes from this jack's own right-click menu
A clock here sets the period that T-RATE and P-RATE divide and multiply, measured from one rising edge to the next
Moves the filter cutoff, ±10V covering the whole sweep, and is read only while the FILT knob's modulation source is set to CV
The left channel, carrying the summed engine after the tremolo, auto-pan, chorus, low-pass filter and limiter, hard clamped to ±10V
The right channel, carrying the summed engine after the tremolo, auto-pan, chorus, low-pass filter and limiter, hard clamped to ±10V
Note — no sound is made until a gate arrives at GATE; a pitch at V/OCT on its own starts nothing
Note — the sixteen voices are summed inside the engine before any of the effects, so L and R carry one mixed signal rather than a polyphonic cable
Note — MOD does nothing until the BARK knob's or the reed drive's modulation source is set to Mod input and its depth is moved off zero
Note — the CV jack does nothing until the FILT knob's modulation source is set to CV and its Mod depth is moved off zero
Note — the display draws the shape set by the A, D, S and R trimpots, with a dot tracking the first polyphonic channel's position along it
Note — the reed drive, the velocity curve, the filter's keytrack and the two modulation depths are not on the panel; they are sliders on the module's menu and on the BARK and FILT knobs' menus
Menu — Amp envelope source: Reed, Envelope — on the VOLUME knob's menu: Reed leaves each note's own reed decay to shape the tail, Envelope multiplies the whole output by the panel envelope
Menu — Modulation source: Envelope, Mod input — on the BARK knob's menu: picks whether the panel envelope or the voltage at MOD moves the bark amount
Menu — Modulation depth — a slider on the BARK knob's menu, -100% to +100%, setting how far the chosen source moves the bark amount
Menu — Modulation source: Envelope, CV — on the FILT knob's menu: picks whether the panel envelope or the voltage at the CV jack moves the cutoff
Menu — Mod depth — a slider on the FILT knob's menu, -100% to +100%, setting how far the chosen source moves the cutoff
Menu — Keytrack — a slider on the FILT knob's menu, 0 to 100%; at 100% the cutoff follows the average pitch of the held notes at one octave per volt
Menu — Bend range: ±2 semitones, ±5 semitones, ±7 semitones, ±12 semitones — on the BEND jack's menu: sets how far ±5V at that jack bends
Menu — Velocity curve: Parabolic, Exponential — Parabolic raises the incoming velocity to a power of 1 to 4, Exponential to a power of 1 down to 0.25, and the slider under them sets how far
Menu — (connect VEL input to enable) — printed where the velocity slider would be when VEL has no cable, and the two curve choices are greyed out while it shows
Menu — Reed drive (gnarl): Envelope, Mod input — picks whether the panel envelope or the voltage at MOD raises the reed level going into the pickup
Menu — Reed drive — a slider setting the reed level into the pickup, one times at the left and four times at the right
Menu — Mod depth — a slider on the module's menu, 0 to 100%, setting how much the chosen source adds to the reed drive

5.why: Wurl.cpp:1034 reads getVoltage() with no channel on every 64th sample, divides it by 5 and multiplies by the menu's semitone count over 12 at line 1040

7.why: Wurl.cpp:1104 reads getVoltage() with no channel, scales it by 0.1 and clamps it to -1 and 1, and line 1109 multiplies that by the Mod depth slider

TC-Wurl.notes: Read from the maker's source at commit 5d573b7, the only commit whose plugin.json carries the installed 2.0.1; the installed binary confirms it, carrying the 4.5V limiter threshold that commit introduced (visible as an fmov of 4.50000000 in the constructor and in onSampleRateChange, where 2.0.0 had 5.0). Params 2, 18, 19, 20, 21 and 22 are configured but no ParamWidget is added for them: they are sliders on the BARK knob's menu (Modulation depth), the FILT knob's menu (Mod depth, Keytrack) and the module's own menu (Velocity curve, Reed drive, Mod depth), so no click on the panel can reach them and they carry no line or tag here. The manual is dated to 2.0.0 and disagrees with the shipped code in two places: it gives the VOLUME default as 70% where configParam sets 0.85, and it calls the reed drive's mod depth bipolar where configParam gives it 0 to 1. MOD is scaled two different ways by the two things that read it — times 0.2 and clamped to ±1 for bark, times 0.1 and clamped to 0 and 1 for reed drive, so a negative voltage swings the bark and is ignored by the reed drive; the manual gives only the ±5V to ±1 mapping. The gate and pedal Schmitt triggers are only advanced on every eighth sample, so a gate shorter than about 170 microseconds at 48kHz can be missed.
